description: Analyze the relationship between FCBoost's static CA-derived mask and Kitty's dynamic magnitude-based channel selection

interpretation.scenario_label: Low mask overlap + FCBoost beats Kitty => static selection works via different mechanism
interpretation.details: Mean Jaccard=0.299 (<=0.5 threshold) indicates the actual 16-channel sets selected by CA and magnitude are largely different. However, mean Spearman=0.670 (>0.5) shows the rankings of RoPE pairs are moderately correlated. FCBoost (71.11%) outperforms Kitty (66.67%) by +4.44pp despite using different channels. This suggests CA identifies structurally important RoPE frequencies for quantization sensitivity that partially correlate with magnitude but select a different (and apparently better) subset of channels.
interpretation.key_insight: CA and magnitude agree on which channels are roughly more important (high rank correlation), but they disagree on the exact top-16 cut (low Jaccard). The CA-derived static selection appears to capture a qualitatively different and more effective set of quantization-sensitive channels.
